title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
abstract: arXiv:2611.13562v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Benchmark scores for medical large language models (LLMs) are difficult to interpret when scoring criteria cannot be traced to clinical evidence. Here we developed Med Evidence Bench (MEB; https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/), comprising 1,536 physician-constructed items across three levels: guideline knowledge, standardized clinical scenarios and real-world laboratory scenarios. Each criterion stating a medical claim is linked to a versioned source-text span. Across ten LLMs, the Evidence Trace Score (ETS) was 0.975-0.997 for guideline knowledge, 0.292-0.658 for standardized scenarios and 0.182-0.447 for real-world scenarios, and rankings varied across levels. For real-world scenarios, scores for identifying clinical information (mean, 0.770) exceeded those for matching evidence (0.165) or formulating recommendations (0.160). translated_abstract: 当评分标准无法追溯到临床证据时，医学大语言模型（LLM）的基准测试分数便难以解读。本研究开发了Med Evidence Bench（MEB；https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/），包含1,536个由医生构建的测试项目，涵盖三个层次：指南知识、标准化临床场景以及真实世界检验（实验室）场景。每条陈述医学论断的评分标准均关联到一个带版本编号的原文文本片段。在十个大语言模型上，证据可追溯分数（Evidence Trace Score, ETS）在指南知识层面为0.975–0.997，在标准化场景层面为0.292–0.658，在真实世界场景层面为0.182–0.447，且各层次间的模型排名存在差异。对于真实世界场景，识别临床信息的得分（平均0.770）高于匹配证据（0.165）或提出建议（0.160）的得分。在1,296条标准层面的评判中，自动评分与三位医生的多数投票结果一致（宏——[原文摘要至此截断]
tldr: 该研究构建了首个证据可追溯的医学大语言模型基准Med Evidence Bench（MEB），将每条评分标准与版本化的文献原文片段绑定，揭示出十个主流大语言模型虽在指南知识上表现优异，但在真实世界临床场景中的推理能力显著下降。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Med Evidence Bench (MEB), an evidence-traceable benchmark linking every scoring criterion to versioned source-text spans, revealing that ten LLMs perform well on guideline knowledge but their clinical reasoning drops sharply on real-world scenarios.
